newsitem.title: NIGER: New Air Afrique boss takes over, targets debt.
newsitem.headline: New Air Afrique boss takes over, targets debt.

text.p: Air Afrique's new managing director, Sir Harry K. Tirvengadum of Mauritius, has taken over the struggling multi-national carrier with an appeal to states that own it to think twice before letting in charter flights.
The former head of Air Mauritius, formally appointed late on Monday in the Niger capital Niamey, says lifting the company's debt burden is his number one priority.
"The tasks that I face are huge but I will devote myself to solving them in order of priority," he told a news conference after his appointment.

"We are in a position of competitive weakness but we will look at how to confront this," he said, adding that he wanted to solve the problem of the airline's 200 billion CFA franc ($350 million) debt by March 31 -- a deadline set by the creditors.

He told Radio France International, in an interview broadcast on Tuesday, he would devote himself to ensuring a leasing company set up with the Francophone Africa air safety agency ASECNA and member states to buy planes at the root of the debt problem would be up and running before the deadline.

At the same time, he appealed to the 11 states that hold a majority stake in Air Afrique to curb inroads into the region made by foreign charter flight companies -- a major cut-price source of competition to Air Afrique.
"There is competition, unbridled competition because there are no competitive rules, but that's the way it is," he said.
Air Afrique's owners see the airline, which was set up in 1961 during the heady days that followed independence, as a symbol of inter-African cooperation.

Sir Harry said he was not against alliances with other airlines. "Every airline company in the world is looking for alliances, even the big companies of America, Africa and Europe are looking for alliances even when they are strong and profitable," he added.

He said it would be a good thing for Air Afrique to look for alliances provided they did not "diminish (its) chances of developing, advancing and increasing its own business network" but he added that he wanted time to consider the issue.
An alliance with French carrier Air France, which has a small stake in Air Afrique, has frequently been mooted.
Sir Harry replaces French chairman and managing director Yves-Roland Billecart whose mandate was cut short by the ministers of the 11 member states.
He said he would hold a meeting shortly in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan, headquarters of the airline, with the staff, who had campaigned for Billecart's departure.
The board elected Niger's transport minister, Souley Abdoulaye, as its chairman.
The airline is majority owned by Benin, Burkina Faso, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Ivory Coast, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Senegal and Togo.
